newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures were called to open little changed Thursday after a lackluster performance in London overnight, traders said.

LIFFE cocoa futures were a touch higher in thin, rangebound dealings early Thursday, with July was up one stg at the midday break at 998 stg a tonne after ranging from 1,000 to 997 stg. Sepember was up the same at 1,016 stg.

Wednesday, New York cocoa futures bounced back after two days of losses to end higher, but dealings were extremely thin. July ended up $13 at $1,422 a tonne after trading from $1,425 to $1,412. Spot May, which expired Wednesday, settled up $27 at $1,427, with the rest rising $12 to $14.

Technically, traders pegged near-term July resistance at a chart gap between $1,425 and $1,428, with the next upside objective noted at $1,437-$1,440. Support was seen toward yesterday's low of $1,412, then $1,400.

On the fundamental front, crop analysts and exporters in Abdijan said on Thursday that the Ivory Coast's mid-crop (May-Sept) could match harvest forecasts of more than 150,000 tonnes but bean sizes were down from the last year's record main season (Oct-Sept). ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
